Next year may see the launch of the largest-screened iPhone ever, according to a leaker with a fairly reliable track record.

Supply chain sources reveal that Apple is testing a new display panel that could be used in a new iPhone whose model name remains a mystery……

The naming mystery of next year's flagship iPhone

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and for years there has been a widespread belief that Apple is preparing something special. It is expected that this year the company will come very close to realising its long-standing iPhone design vision — "a single slab of glass".

Some believe Apple may launch a standalone 20th-anniversary edition iPhone, similar to the iPhone X of its day. However, more recent reports suggest that this groundbreaking new device will be released directly as next year's Pro model — namely the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

A third possibility is that Apple will skip directly from the iPhone 18 to the iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary.

The largest iPhone screen ever

Leaker "Digital Chat Station" (DCS) says supply chain information indicates Apple is testing the largest iPhone screen to date. However, compared with the existing 6.9-inch iPhone 17 Pro Max, the increase in size is relatively modest.

In other words, they believe Apple will market it as a 7-inch screen.

DCS does not have information on what this new screen will be used for — assuming Apple ultimately brings it to fruition — but he speculates it may be used in next year's iPhone Pro Max, whatever brand name that model ultimately adopts.

9to5Mac's perspective

Apple tests all sorts of things, most of which never actually make it to market, so even if this screen prototype does exist in the supply chain, it does not necessarily mean it will end up in an iPhone.

That said, if Apple's goal is to deliver a "single slab of glass" effect, then billing it as the largest screen ever does seem like a rather reasonable marketing angle.
